rv.q: In this hauntingly beautiful and structurally daring solo work, creator, writer and performer Jared Mezzocchi transforms autobiography into a form of celestial archaeology.

The scope of the show is contained in the contrast between the enveloping sweep of the sky in a planetarium dome and the more mundane imagery, the fussy domesticity of the snapshots and of Jared’s hands on the buttons of a cassette recorder.
After a while, his performance becomes plodding, and his replication of Rosemary’s Yankee-accented voice is not persuasive.
Still, 73 Seconds remains worth seeing for its immersive experience alone.

cn.t: Mezzocchi's intimate solo work about his mother's NASA connection and dementia receives mostly positive notices for its haunting exploration of memory and loss, though some find the ambitious piece more atmospheric than narratively cohesive.
